result.note: Tests the RBI's BRICS CBDC-linking proposal, its CBDC-over-stablecoin stance, and the Rio de Janeiro declaration it builds on.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about a proposal made by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in January 2026:
items: It seeks to link BRICS members' central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) to ease cross-border trade and tourism payments.
The RBI recommended that it be placed on the agenda of the 2026 BRICS Summit, which India will host.
The RBI favours private stablecoins over CBDCs because stablecoins strengthen capital controls.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The third statement is wrong. The RBI prefers CBDCs to private stablecoins, citing risks of de-facto dollarisation and weakened capital controls. Digital rails are being pitched as a workaround after rupee trade settlement with Russia stalled.
questions.source: The RBI prefers central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) to private stablecoins, citing risks of de-facto dollarisation and weakened capital controls.

questions.prompt: In January 2026, the RBI proposed linking BRICS central bank digital currencies, building on a 2025 BRICS declaration that called for greater interoperability between members' payment systems. In which city was that 2025 declaration adopted?
questions.explain: The proposal flows from the 2025 BRICS declaration in Rio de Janeiro. India, which hosts the 2026 summit, presents BRICS as a payments and trade platform rather than a geopolitical alliance.
questions.source: The idea flows from the 2025 BRICS declaration in Rio de Janeiro, which called for greater interoperability between member countries’ payment systems.
